A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LMAct study and contain readable main text and appendices. Figures, tables, and prompt listings can be matched despite reordering and pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C report original model evaluations, replay controls, and prompting ablations across six interactive environments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark performance curves, replay experiments, and the ablation tables.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Listings 1–2 retain the same demonstration conditioning, action generation, trajectory history, prompting options, and illegal-action handling. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Phoenix, chess, crosswords, Cheetah Run, grid navigation, and tic-tac-toe with the same observation formats. Robotics transfer and partially observable tasks are discussed as future directions, without additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same eight frontier models and task-specific random and expert references. The newly cited control methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain 100 evaluation episodes, the same demonstration sampling, output budgets, initial-condition controls, metrics, and prompt-selection procedures. The methods text is unchanged apart from line wrapping.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the output-length, replay, illegal-action, prompting, and past-action analyses. The new future-work discussion refers to these existing investigations without adding experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Episode and seed information, averaging over 100 evaluation episodes, and statistical reporting remain unchanged. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Matched performance plots, replay heatmaps, and Tables A1–A16 retain their results. The Cheetah Run and tic-tac-toe figures are renumbered, and Table A2 is relocated without changing its entries.

T1.justification: No formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs change. The new discussion of self-delusion under partial observability cites prior work conceptually rather than introducing mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contributions, and conclusion retain the same benchmark scope and central claims: models often fall short of expert performance, and additional demonstrations frequently provide little benefit.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds qualifications about real-world transfer and partial observability, including self-delusion concerns. It discusses existing performance declines as in-context interference, links them to suboptimal actions, and explicitly leaves their definitive cause unresolved.

D1.justification: Model/API constraints, prompt templates, demonstration selection and processing, hyperparameters, and code/data access information are retained. Relocated experimental details do not introduce technical revisions.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds literature on prompting, memory-based long-context models, BABILong, and in-context control. It explicitly distinguishes specialized agent development from benchmarking existing general-purpose models, extending the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized copyedits, updates publication and bibliographic metadata, expands the discussion and related work, and reorders task discussions. Appendix C.4.1's previously fragmented explanation is consolidated; most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained. Tic-tac-toe changes from Figure 8 to Figure 6, Cheetah Run changes from Figure 6 to Figure 8, and Table A2 moves from v2 page 22 to v3 page 25. These are layout changes without redrawn plots.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies transfer and observability limits and better situates LMAct relative to specialized agent research. Consolidating Appendix C.4.1 also repairs an explanation split across widely separated pages in v2. These provide limited gains in interpretation and readability; the experimental evidence and principal conclusions remain unchanged.
